newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL tin ends down 19 cents, tracks London's fall.
newsitem.headline: KL tin ends down 19 cents, tracks London's fall.

text.p: Malaysia's tin price ended down 19 cents at 14.72 ringgit ($5.83) a kg, moving in tandem with the London Metal Exchange (LME) where tin prices fell to an 18-month low on Monday, traders said.
"The local market was reacting to the fall in LME but the drop here was not as bad as expected. I think market players are anticipating a sharp rebound in LME today," said one trader.

He said the fall in London overnight was overdone and a technical rebound is expected. LME tin price hit $5,810 on Monday, the lowest since May 19, 1995, before closing at $5,840, down $180 from Friday.
Traders said that although further losses in London could weigh on the local price, strong support is expected at 14.50 ringgit.
Turnover was 95 tonnes, down from 108 on Monday, and buyers were from Europe, Japan and Malaysia, traders said.
The local price premium over the LME widened to $135 a tonne against $45 on Monday following the sharp drop in London, the traders said.
